# OUSD(R&E) Developmental Test and Evaluation of Autonomous Systems Guidebook

> **External, not NASA governance.** Useful for comparison and vocabulary. It never establishes
> what NASA requires, and must not be cited as NASA coverage.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Publisher / owner** | Office of the Director, Developmental Test, Evaluation, and Assessments (DTEA); Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering (OUSD(R&E)) |
| **Kind** | Guidebook (DoD T&E community guidance) |
| **Status** | September 2025 edition. DOPSR Case # 25-T-3068. |
| **Where to get it** | Public: cto.mil/dtea; Distribution Statement A, approved for public release, distribution unlimited. Public copy, confirmed anonymously off-network on 2026-10-26: `https://www.cto.mil/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/DTE-of-AS-GB.pdf` |
| **Binds whom** | DoD independent government test teams planning and executing autonomous-systems T&E (Executive Summary, p.iii) — guidance for DoD programs, not a NASA/JPL document. |

**What it is good for, relative to NASA's documents.** A DoD-specific counterpart for
autonomy assurance, addressing "the novel challenges of removing or greatly reducing involvement of
human operators" (Executive Summary, p.iii, verbatim) — useful vocabulary and framing for autonomy
T&E, distinct from the companion AI-Enabled Systems guidebook's narrower AI focus (our reading).

**Key content for AI / machine-learning assurance.**
- States four intents (Executive Summary, p.iii, verbatim list): identify and explain DoD policy for
  autonomous-systems T&E; identify and explain overarching and specific T&E challenges; share guidance
  on methods/best practices across "the full continuum of autonomy T&E"; provide tool/resource
  information from trusted federal sources.
- Frames autonomy as an "emerging technology" requiring guidance that "will be updated as technology and
  methodologies evolve" (Executive Summary, p.iii, paraphrase).
- A text search of the public PDF finds roughly 53 occurrences of "artificial intelligence"/"machine learning" —
  the guidebook treats autonomy and AI/ML as overlapping but distinct topics (our reading; exact overlap
  not itemized here).

**Nearest NASA counterpart.** No NASA document is dedicated to autonomy-specific T&E in this way;
compares to `../documents/NPR_8705.4B.md` (risk classification) and `../documents/NPR_7120.5F.md`
(program management, including T&E planning) (our reading, comparison only).
